entries.description_markdown: Hewitt discusses Ovine by Design, the tools used to make its PC remakes, and its remake of **Imogen**.
The emulator author discusses DreamSpec and DC64, including hardware differences that affect emulator development.
Nishikado discusses the design of **Space Invaders** and its later anniversary edition.
Ullyatt discusses Cronosoft, a publisher of new games for older computers. Jonathan Cauldwell and his games are covered in the feature, but Cauldwell is not the interviewee.
Dini discusses the design of **Kick Off** and **Goal!**.
Singleton discusses the design and development of **The Lords of Midnight** series in a history of the trilogy.
The Protovision team discusses Commodore 64 development, including **Metal Dust**, **Tanks 3000**, and **Pac It**.
Fotheringham discusses the unreleased **Mega-tree**, his work at Software Projects and Denton Designs, and surviving development disks.
The Desert Island Disks profile discusses Adams's early adventure games and his approach to writing them.
White discusses the development of **Ant Attack** and **I of the Mask**.
Harlow discusses the history of 1632 Systems, its Atari ST public-domain library, and JagFest UK.
Bushnell discusses Atari and his views on the games industry.
The Desert Island Disks profile discusses Doak's work on **GoldenEye 007** at Rare and his move to Free Radical Design.
Warriner discusses Revolution Software and the development of its adventure games, including **Broken Sword**.
Keating discusses developing **Skools Out**, a PC game inspired by **Skool Daze**.
A collection of Smith's comments and Q&A answers at CGE UK covers **Manic Miner**, **Jet Set Willy**, and his career.
Needle discusses developing the **Spectaculator** emulator and its RZX recording support.
Lionet discusses creating **STOS**, **AMOS**, and later game-authoring tools.
Maegawa discusses founding Treasure after working at Konami and the studio's approach to its games.
The Desert Island Disks profile discusses **Dropzone**, **International Karate**, and Maclean's arcade-machine collection.
AEG discusses the development of **Turrican 3** for the Commodore 64.
Turner gives a first-person history of Graftgold, including its development methods and later games.
Meretzky discusses his work at Infocom in an interview accompanying a history of the company, including **Planetfall**, **Sorcerer**, and **The Hitchhiker's Guide to the Galaxy**.
Evans discusses developing **Trashman** and its sequels, including the technical limits of the Spectrum.
Former Color Dreams staff discuss the company's unlicensed NES games and its later Wisdom Tree releases.

entries.developer: Robert White, Mike Richardson, and Clive Townsend
entries.description_markdown: The founder and programmers of Durell discuss the publisher's early games and development work.
Crane discusses programming for the Atari 2600, leaving Atari to form Activision, and **Pitfall!**.
The Desert Island Disks profile covers Mosaic Publishing and its licensed game adaptations.
Minter discusses Llamasoft's games, including **Attack of the Mutant Camels** and **Gridrunner++**.
Yarusso discusses AtariAge, its game archive, and the Atari homebrew community.
The Desert Island Disks profile discusses Fenton's work on **GORF** and the Bally Arcade.
Gollop discusses **Chaos**, **Lords of Chaos**, **Laser Squad**, and **X-Com**.
Kulczycki discusses disassembling and modifying arcade game ROMs.
Heckendorn discusses building portable versions of game consoles.
Elite Systems co-founder Wilcox discusses the company's games, licences, and business history.
Ritman discusses **Match Day**, **Batman**, and **Head Over Heels**.
The Desert Island Disks profile covers Ginner's work on Lynx and Jaguar games.
McNeill discusses Delta 4's parody adventure games and how they were made.
The Desert Island Disks feature covers their work creating **Digitiser**.
Gilsoft founder Gilberts and programmer Yeandle discuss **The Quill**, **PAW**, and adventure game authoring tools.
The Desert Island Disks profile covers Carruthers's programming career, including **Xor** and **Archipelagos**.
The creators of **Skool Daze** discuss its programming, art, and school setting.
The Desert Island Disks profile discusses Skelly's arcade programming, including **Reactor**.
Crane discusses the design and development of **Little Computer People**.
Cale discusses designing **The Last Ninja** and the series' later games.
Twiddy discusses programming **The Last Ninja** series.
Glu Mobile's head of game development discusses adapting **The Chaos Engine** for mobile phones.
Amsoft's former technical manager discusses its software publishing strategy.
Lowe discusses creating and developing the **Leisure Suit Larry** games.
The Magnetic Fields co-founders discuss their games, including **Lotus Turbo Challenge** and **Super Cars**.
Hollis discusses directing **Perfect Dark** at Rare.
The Desert Island Disks profile covers the brothers' early programming and artwork.
Robertson discusses the process of creating loading-screen artwork.
Former American Technos executive Rice discusses the company's arcade and home-game releases.
The second part of their Desert Island Disks profile covers their later work and game choices.
Roper discusses making a **Horace and the Spiders** remake for the Retro Ball competition.
Bushnell discusses founding Atari, developing Pong, and his views on early and modern game design.
The Team17 lookback uses Brown and Dyson's recollections of its Amiga development, publishing decisions, and the arrival of Worms.
Trenz explains the design and technical challenges behind the original Turrican.
The Desert Island Disks profile covers Davis's work on Q*bert, digitised graphics, and later arcade games.
Cakebread discusses the creation of Geometry Wars and its Xbox Live Arcade sequel.
A short interview in the emulation feature covers Bannister's work porting emulators to Mac OS X.
Ellis and Gregory explain the Freescape engine, Driller, and later games.
Purcell discusses the characters and development of Sam & Max Hit the Road.
Schafer discusses joining Lucasfilm Games and creating adventure games including The Secret of Monkey Island and Grim Fandango.
Caswell explains the design and programming of Impossible Mission.
The US Gold founder recounts the company's origins, imports, publishing, and relationships with developers.
Turner explains the design of Quazatron and its isometric engine.
The Desert Island Disks profile covers Liddon's work at Zzap!64, Thalamus, and later game studios.
A short Q&A covers his Total Eclipse and Wizball remake projects.
Davidson recounts how Total Wormage became Worms and how he developed its characters and play mechanics.

entries.developer: Gary Bracey and former Ocean staff
entries.description_markdown: Former Ocean staff discuss the studio's games, licensing, production, and working conditions.
The Bloodwych feature includes James's recollections of developing the two-player role-playing game.
Porter describes Gremlin Graphics' home conversions of Gauntlet and the constraints of each machine.
The Palace Software founders recount the company's origins, development, publishing, and Barbarian.

entries.developer: Trip Hawkins, Joe Ybarra, and Jim Rushing
entries.description_markdown: Contributors to M.U.L.E. discuss its design, playtesting, publishing, and commercial reception.
The Desert Island Disks profile covers Evans's work on 3D Monster Maze, Trashman, and other games.
A developer lookback uses staff recollections to trace Gremlin Graphics and its games.
Chahi discusses creating Another World, including its animation and cinematic presentation.
Goldman discusses the animation and production of Dragon's Lair.
A short Q&A with the Dragon's Lair Project creator covers his archive and preservation of laserdisc arcade games.
Hawkins discusses founding Electronic Arts and his approach to the games business.
Frey discusses creating cover and game art for Crash, Zzap!64, and other publications.
The Desert Island Disks profile covers Jarvis's arcade design work, including Defender and Robotron: 2084.
Lamb and Bracey explain the development of Target: Renegade.
Cuthbert gives developer insight into the cancellation of Star Fox 2.
Crane recounts leaving Atari and the founding and early development practices of Activision.
The creators of Maximum magazine discuss its design and why it lasted seven issues.
Crane explains how the Ghostbusters game was made and adapted from the film.
Former Hi-Tec Software staff discuss licensed cartoon games, production, and the small studio's work.
The Desert Island Disks profile covers Warshaw's Atari games and later career.
The Retro Remakes site owner discusses its competition and the homebrew remake community.
Naka contributes to a Sonic Team lookback covering its games and studio history.
Maclean explains how he developed International Karate and IK+.
Axelsson discusses DICE's Pinball Dreams, Pinball Fantasies, and Pinball Illusions.
The Desert Island Disks profile covers Pelling's programming career, including Frak!.
Liepa discusses creating Boulder Dash and its movement and level design.

entries.developer: David Fox, Noah Falstein, and LucasArts staff
entries.description_markdown: The first LucasArts lookback uses developer recollections to cover its early games and technology.
DeSharone discusses making Link: The Faces of Evil and Zelda: The Wand of Gamelon.
Jones recounts creating the Magic Knight adventure games for Mastertronic.
Day discusses converting the Hard Drivin' arcade game for home computers.
The Desert Island Disks profile covers Polaro's work at Commodore and Atari and his Atari 2600 games.
The Retro Fusion organiser discusses the event, its arcade hardware, guests, and plans for the year.
The second LucasArts lookback draws on developer recollections of its adventure games and later work.
San explains Argonaut's work with Nintendo on Star Fox and the Super FX chip.
Hawkins discusses the design, launch, licensing, and fortunes of the 3DO Interactive Multiplayer.
Wozniak recounts designing Breakout hardware for Atari.
The NG:Dev.Team brothers discuss making and publishing Last Hope for Neo Geo.
A company profile uses former staff recollections to cover Core Design and the creation of Tomb Raider.
Baer discusses developing the Brown Box and the beginnings of home video games.
Cobb explains the translation, bug fixes, and release of Beggar Prince.
Palmer describes adapting Usagi Yojimbo into Samurai Warrior and designing its combat and karma systems.
A Q&A with developers including Simon Butler, the Oliver twins, Ste Pickford, Jon Ritman, and Bill Harbison reflects on Spectrum development.
The Capcom developers discuss the Ghosts 'n Goblins series and its design.
A Q&A in the Oric-1 retrospective covers Tansoft software and the machine's early publishing scene.
Darling discusses Codemasters' origins, games, publishing, and later direction.
Whittaker discusses programming Lazy Jones and composing its music.
The Desert Island Disks profile covers Logg's work on Asteroids, Centipede, Gauntlet, and other arcade games.
Irvin discusses the design and technical constraints of Exile.
Riordan recounts developing It Came from the Desert and its cinematic presentation.
The Tec Toy president discusses the company's Sega partnership, Brazilian releases, and localisation.
The Desert Island Disks profile covers Ellis's GoldenEye multiplayer work and Free Radical Design.
Sobodash discusses fan translation tools and work on Beggar Prince and Heroine Anthem.
Discusses the development of **Impossible Mission** for **DS** and **PSP**, noting the effective use of the touch screen in the **DS** version and the superior visuals of the **PSP** version.
Known for co-founding **Team 17**, creators of the **Worms** series and other **Amiga** classics
Discusses the development of **Alter Ego**, a 'life simulator' released by **Activision** in **1986**.
Discusses the development of **Pokémon** for the **Game Boy**, mentioning his mentorship under Shigeru Miyamoto and the naming of characters Ash and Shigeru after himself and Miyamoto.
Discusses his isometric adventure game **Head Over Heels**.
Discusses the history of **System 3**, including their past titles and plans for the future. The company is known for titles like **Impossible Mission** and **The Last Ninja**
Discusses the creation of **Monkey Island**, including the game's development process and his collaboration with Tim Schafer and Dave Grossman
Discusses his work at **Zenobi**, a company he founded to create text-based adventure games, including **Arrival on the Atari ST**, **An Everyday Tale Of A Seeker Of Gold**, and **Fuddo And Slam**.
Discusses his time at **Atari**
Discusses a new retro game competition he is involved in, seeking new ideas inspired by classic titles like **Pac-Man**, **Space Invaders**, and **Tank Wars**.
Discusses the making of **Pitfall II: Lost Caverns**
Discuss their updated version of **California Games**, which includes **Summer Games 1 and 2**
Discuss the making of **Jetpac Refuelled** for **Xbox Live Arcade**
Discuss the creation of **Lemmings**
Discuss the development of **Libble Rabble**
Discusses his time at **id Software** and the development of **Quake**, including his design philosophy and his eventual departure from the company to form **Ion Storm**.
Discusses his work on **Cad Cam Warrior** and **Super Pipeline 2**
Discusses his entry into the gaming industry as a QA tester for **Team17** on **Worms**, and his eventual role as lead producer on **Worms: Open Warfare 2**
Discusses the creation of **Tetris**
Discuss what inspired them to create a shoot 'em up game like **Söldner-X** for the **PlayStation 3**
Discuss their work at **Llamasoft**, including the development of **Space Giraffe** for **Xbox Live Arcade** and their plans for future titles like **Sheep in Space** and **Ancipital**
Discusses the creation of **Sensible Soccer** for the **Amiga**
Discuss the development of **Fort Apocalypse**
Discusses the creation of **Treasure Island Dizzy**
Discuss the making of **NiGHTS into Dreams** and its sequel, **Journey of Dreams** for the **Wii**
Discusses his adventure game **Loom**
Discuss the creation of **California Games**
Discusses his contributions to the gaming industry, including his work on simulation games like **SimCity** and **The Sims**
Discusses the making of his seminal platformer **Manic Miner**
Discusses his type-in game, **Andre's Night Off**, which he coded in BASIC for **Computer & Video Games** magazine, and mentions his work on **Manic Miner**, **Jet Set Willy**, and **Styx**
Discuss their game **Tavern RPG**
Discusses the creation of **Retro Gamer** magazine
Discuss the games that changed their lives, including **Tir Na Nog** and **Jet Set Willy**
Discuss the making of **R-Type Delta** for the original **PlayStation**

Discusses the upcoming **Retro Fusion** event and the guests who will be in attendance, including **Archer MacLean, Andy Nuttal, Jon Hare, Martin Hollis, Alex Trowers, Simon Goodwin**, and **Ste Pickford**.

Chris Gibbs was one of the founding members of Attention To Detail, a game development company. He worked with Jon Steele and Martin on a conversion of *Super Sprint* for the Atari ST. After this project, they were commisioned by LucasArts to make PC, Atari ST, Amiga, Commodore 64, Spectrum, and Amstrad versions of *Night Shift*.
Fred Gill was one of the founding members of Attention To Detail. Before forming the company with Chris Gibbs, Jon Steele, and Jon Dean, his Spectrum shooter *Octan* was published by Firebird.

Jon Dean was a producer for Activision. While there, he met Chris Gibbs, Fred Gill, and Jon Steele. They created a conversion of *Super Sprint* for the Atari ST. Dean proposed the group start a company called Attention To Detail that would work exclusively with PMC.
Jon Steele was one of the founding members of Attention To Detail. He worked with Chris Gibbs and Martin on a conversion of *Super Sprint* for the Atari ST.
Hideo Kojima is a game designer known for his work on the *Metal Gear* series. He has stated a desire to direct a film.
Eugene Lacey was involved with *Computer & Video Games* magazine during the 1980s.
Jim Levy was involved with the founding of Activision. He understood the desire among developers to receive credit for their work.
Jon Hare co-founded Sensible Software, the company behind *Sensible Soccer*. He has also worked at Argonaut Games.
Issue 60 of *Retro Gamer* featured an interview with Trevor Storey.
Jeff Minter is a game developer.
Matthew Smith was a game developer.
Tony Crowther developed the games *Blagger* and *Burnout Paradise*.
Toru Iwatani is the creator of *Pac-Man*. In this issue, he discusses rebooting the franchise for Xbox Live Arcade.
Tomohiro Nishikado is the creator of *Space Invaders*.
Trip Hawkins is the founder Electronic Arts (EA). He discusses EA's role in the success of the Sega Mega Drive.
Archer Maclean developed *Dropzone*, which he showed to Atari UK in 1982.
Charles Cecil co-founded Revolution Software. He discusses the founding of the studio and how the Wii and DS were revitalizing point-and-click games.
Harri Tikkanen created the *Super Stardust* series, including *Super Stardust HD* for the PS3.
Kevin Toms created the *Football Manager* series.
Ally Noble worked at Denton Designs on a game about the pop band Frankie Goes To Hollywood.
Jamie Woodhouse is a game developer who worked on *Qwak* for Team 17 and *Nitro* for Psygnosis.
John Twiddy developed *Last Ninja* and *Putty Squad*. He also worked on the Konix Multisystem.
Mev Dinc created the Spectrum version of *The Last Ninja*.
Simon Goodwin worked at Ocean, Denton Designs, and Beyond Software.
Issue 66 of *Retro Gamer* featured an interview with Trip Hawkins. He talked about his game *Crazy Penguin Catapult*.
Charles Cecil co-founded Revolution Software and talked about their work on *Lure Of The Temptress* and *Broken Sword: Director's Cut*.
Jon Hare co-founded Sensible Software. He discussed the development of *Shoot-'Em-Up Construction Kit* for the C64.
Gary Bracey worked at Ocean Software, where he oversaw more than 104 games. Notable releases he worked on include *Batman: The Movie* and *Head Over Heels*.
Issue 68 of *Retro Gamer* featured an interview with Hideo Kojima.
Geoff Crammond developed *Super Invaders*, *Aviator*, *Revs*, *The Sentinel*, and *Stunt Car Racer*. His *Grand Prix* series is his most notable work.
James worked at Digital Integration and NovaLogic. He developed the *Die Hard Trilogy* game, which was released for Playstation, Saturn, and PC. This was his first published game.
Simon Pick worked at The Sales Curve, Probe Entertainment, and Digital Integration. He developed the *Die Hard Trilogy* game, which was released for Playstation, Saturn, and PC.
Takeshi Arakawa is the game director of *Dissidia: Final Fantasy*.
Issue 70 of *Retro Gamer* featured an interview with Jon Hare of Sensible Software.
Jeff Minter discussed his work on games including *Defender 2000*, *Revenge Of The Mutant Camels*, and *Trip-A-Tron*. He also mentioned disliking working on *Defender 2000*.
Issue 71 of *Retro Gamer* featured an interview with an unnamed developer who converted *After Burner* to the Commodore 64.
Peter Molyneux worked on *Castle Crashers* and *Braid*.
John Gibson worked at Imagine, where he was involved with the *Bandersnatch* project.
Philip Oliver is the co-creator of the *Dizzy* series.
Stephen Crow created the game *Starquake*.
Tony Oakden worked as the lead programmer on **Driver**.
Issue 73 of *Retro Gamer* featured an interview with Martin Hollis, the director and producer of **GoldenEye 007** and **Perfect Dark**.
Jon Burton designed and programmed the game *Leander*. He was also involved in the development of the *LEGO* games, *Sonic the Hedgehog*, and *Crash Bandicoot*.
Jon Hare co-founded Sensible Software, the company that developed *Sensible World of Soccer*, *Cannon Fodder*, *Mega Lo Mania*, *Wizball*, and *Wizkid*.
Dave Grossman co-created *The Secret of Monkey Island* and *Day of the Tentacle*.
Robert Weatherby was involved with the development of *RoadBlasters*.
Steve Bristow was involved in the development of *Pong*, *Tank*, and *Computer Space*.
John Romero worked at id Software on *Wolfenstein 3D* and *Doom*. He was responsible for programming many of the interactive elements in *Doom*.
Dave Lebling co-created the text adventure, *Zork*.
Ste Pickford worked on the game *Zub* with his brother, Jon.
Roland Perry worked for Tynesoft, where he designed the motherboard for the Amstrad CPC.
Steve Lycett worked on *Sega All-Stars Racing*.
Issue 78 of *Retro Gamer* featured an interview with Yu Suzuki.
Alex Trowers worked at Bullfrog on games such as *Populous* and *Theme Park*. He also worked at Black Rock Studio on *Split/Second*.
David Crane co-founded Activision.
Richard Hanson co-founded Superior Software.
Eric Schwartz created public domain cartoons for the Amiga.
Larry DeMar was involved in the development of *Robotron: 2084* and *Defender*.
Violet Berlin was a presenter on the video game TV shows *Bad Influence* and *Gamepad*.
Jamie developed the arcade game *Gorf*.
Andrew developed the game *Druid*.
Jez San founded Argonaut Software and worked on the game *Starglider*.
Ste Pickford co-developed the game *Zub* with his brother, Jon. He has also worked on titles in the *Plok!* series.
Interview with John Szczepaniak about the creation of *Resident Evil* for the Game Boy Advance.
Issue 89 of *Retro Gamer* features an interview with the developers of *Sprint 2*, Lyle Rains and Dennis Koble.
Steve Turner worked for Graftgold and was involved in the creation of several ZX80, Dragon 32, Commodore 64, and Atari ST games.
Issue 94 of *Retro Gamer* contains an interview with Nick Humphries, the creator of *Your Sinclair: Rock 'N' Roll Years*.
Issue 95 of *Retro Gamer* includes an interview with Matthew Smith about the creation of *Alien Trilogy*.
Shaun Hollingworth worked at Teque London and developed the Commodore 64 game *Firelord*.
Issue 95 of *Retro Gamer* features an interview with Slvye Ybarra, who discusses his time working on *Project Firestart*.

David Leitch worked for The Stamper brothers and was involved in the development of games for the Spectrum, such as *Double Dragon*. He also completed freelance work for Tiertex and converted *Rainbow Islands* for them.
Issue 96 of *Retro Gamer* includes an interview with the developers of *Radiant Silvergun*.
Greg Omi reveals how he ported Klax from the Arcade to the Atari Lynx
Paul Norman discusses the making of Aztec Challenge for the Commodore 64
